final_answer:
A STACK IS A DATA STRUCTURE THAT OPERATES ON THE LIFO (LAST IN, FIRST OUT) PRINCIPLE. THE LAST ITEM ADDED IS THE FIRST TO BE REMOVED. A QUEUE OPERATES ON FIFO (FIRST IN, FIRST OUT), WHERE THE FIRST ITEM ADDED IS THE FIRST TO BE REMOVED. 

A REAL-WORLD EXAMPLE OF A STACK IS A BROWSER'S BACK BUTTON. EACH WEBPAGE VISITED IS PUSHED INTO THE STACK, AND CLICKING BACK REMOVES (POPS) THE MOST RECENT PAGE. 

A REAL-WORLD EXAMPLE OF A QUEUE IS A BANK'S WAITING LINE. CUSTOMERS JOIN THE QUEUE (ENQUEUE) AND ARE SERVED IN THE ORDER THEY ARRIVED (DEQUEUE).
